caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:apl-1
attempts.entry_title: Spiral attractor in the Aplysia pedal ganglion (Bruno, Frost and Humphries 2017)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings hold up in this data: Aplysia pedal ganglion activity forms a low-dimensional periodic orbit, sequential bouts fall on the same manifold, and single neurons vary widely in participation. Convergence within one oscillation period did not hold up, as only 12 of 30 responses reached high recurrence that fast. Motor output was decoded in 8 of the 9 responses with nerve recordings, not all nine. The stable spiral held for the grand mean but not in every preparation, and the caudo-lateral location of strongly participating neurons could not be tested, as the data do not give the array's orientation. Several outcomes depend on a kernel width and dimension count the Methods leave unclear.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Bruno, Frost and Humphries (2017) on CRCNS data set apl-1, which holds the spike times of 30 voltage-sensitive dye recordings of the pedal ganglion (three evoked bouts of fictive locomotion in each of 10 preparations), the P10 nerve spikes of nine of them and the neurons' positions on the photodiode array. It ports the paper's recurrence analysis, local linear models, manifold comparisons, P10 decoding, participation measures and ensemble typing from the paper's MATLAB code, under every reading of the kernel width and the number of dimensions.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Bruno, Frost and Humphries (2017) from CRCNS apl-1

outcomes.statement: Three bouts of fictive locomotion were evoked in each of 10 isolated preparations (30 population responses); each recorded population held 120 to 180 neurons, 1131 neurons in all.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 1; Figure 7B legend
outcomes.quote: We sequentially evoked three bouts of fictive locomotion in each of 10 isolated central nervous system preparations ... Recorded populations from the pedal ganglion comprised 120–180 neurons each
outcomes.notes: 10 preparations, 30 recordings and 1131 neurons, all as the paper gives. Recordings hold 75 to 160 neurons and only 12 of 30 lie in 108 to 198 (120 to 180 widened by 10%), as the data set's description (75 to 160) says. Counting only neurons that spike after onset gives the same numbers. The paper's range cannot hold with its total, as ten preparations of at least 120 neurons would hold at least 1200.

outcomes.statement: After stimulation the spike-train power spectra of the populations are dominated by a slow oscillation at or below 0.1 Hz.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 1; Figure 1D
outcomes.quote: A dominant, slow ( ≤ 0.1 Hz) oscillation in neural firing ( Figure 1D ) is consistent with the periodic activity necessary to generate rhythmic locomotion
outcomes.notes: Power-weighted peak of the grand mean spectrum 0.0486 Hz; per recording 0.0131 to 0.0789 Hz, 30 of 30 above 0 and at or below 0.11 Hz. Variant, frequency of maximum power above 0 Hz, 0.0076 to 0.0992 Hz, 30 of 30 at or below 0.11 Hz. The frequency grid step is 0.0076 Hz. The grand mean spectrum's maximum is at the lowest bin and the spectrum is nearly flat over its first bins (7.54 at 0.0076 Hz, 7.24 at 0.053 Hz), so the decay of the rate contributes to it. A detrended check, not judged, shows an oscillation besides the decay. With a quadratic trend removed from the population rate after offset, the frequency of maximum power above 0.02 Hz is 0.034 to 0.156 Hz (median 0.064 Hz), at or below 0.11 Hz in 27 of 30, and the power in 0.05 to 0.11 Hz exceeds that in 0.2 to 1 Hz in 30 of 30 (median ratio 9.8).
deviations: Chronux mtspectrumpt is ported to Python (apl.mtspectrumpt) with its defaults, tapers [3 5], the time grid from the first to the last spike, the mean rate subtracted; it was not checked against MATLAB output.

outcomes.statement: The population firing rate decays slowly after the stimulus, decreasing in most evoked responses.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 1; Figure 1E (cited as Figure 1F in the text); Results, Heterogenous population activity arises from a common attractor, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: the slowly decaying population firing rate ( Figure 1F ) post-stimulus ... corresponding to the decreasing population spike rate in most evoked responses ( Figure 1E )
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), 30 of 30 decreasing (R from -0.992 to -0.774) and none increasing; reading (b), 30 of 30 negative slopes. Every preparation has three decreasing responses.

outcomes.statement: Capturing 80% of the population variance needs 4 to 8 embedding dimensions in the evoked responses, a reduction by more than a factor of 10 from the number of neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity forms a low-dimensional periodic orbit, paragraph 1; Figure 2B and inset
outcomes.quote: Capturing a significant proportion (80%) of the population variance generally required 4–8 embedding dimensions ( Figure 2B ), representing a dimension reduction by more than a factor of 10 compared to the number of neurons
outcomes.notes: Reproduced under reading (c) with the recording's own median ISI and count (ii), at most 80% (own/le80), the first reading the criterion lists that matches; 28 of 30 counts in 3.6 to 8.8 (3 to 7) and neurons divided by count above 10 in all 30 (lowest 10.7). The code's pooled median with count (ii) gives the same 28 and 30. With count (i), smallest reaching 80%, the counts are 4 to 8 (the paper's range; 30 of 30 in range) but the ratio is 9.4 in one recording (75 neurons, 8 PCs), so the criterion fails there by one response. The readings (a) median ISI / sqrt(12) and (b) median ISI / 12 give 21 to 76 dimensions and ratios of 1.8 to 2.8 at the lowest. The adopted reading of the later claims (own/min80) is one under which this claim fails, by one response.
deviations: The kernel width is read four ways (median ISI / sqrt(12), / 12, the median ISI of the recording, and the code's running median over the recordings of the same bout number), each with both count rules, as the criterion lists.

outcomes.statement: The evoked low-dimensional activity recurs with a regular period; strongly periodic recurrence on the scale of 10 to 15 s is found in many but not all of the 30 responses.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity forms a low-dimensional periodic orbit, paragraph 3; Figure 2D to 2F
outcomes.quote: We found strongly periodic recurrence on the scale of 10–15 s in many but not all of the 30 evoked population responses ( Figure 2E,F )
outcomes.notes: Measured gives the quartiles of the 30 dominant periods under the adopted reading (own/min80, mean of the peak). 26 of 30 periods lie in 9 to 16.5 s, and 4 do not (17.28, 22.23, 8.75 and 19.94 s); with the median of the peak 23 of 30. The four readings with the code's width give 22 to 26 of 30, the narrow widths 13 to 29; every reading except twelve/le80 with the mean (13 of 30) meets the criterion.
deviations: Recurrence follows Analyse_by_Recurrence_Points.m (points from 35 s to 10 s before the end, the first contiguous run within theta dropped, bins of 1 s on 0 to 50 s, peaks of at least 100 points), as the claims file's opening comment gives it.

outcomes.statement: Almost all populations are dominated by a single periodic orbit; the majority of programs have more than 50% of their recurrent points in the dominant peak.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity forms a low-dimensional periodic orbit, paragraph 3; Materials and methods, Recurrence analysis, paragraph 3; Figure 2E
outcomes.quote: the majority of programs had more than 50% of their recurrent points in this peak (blue-scale vectors in Figure 2E )
outcomes.notes: Adopted reading, 29 of 30 responses above 50% with delays of 5 to 50 s, 27 of 30 counting all recurrent points (propInMaxPeriod). 1 to 4 peaks per response (12 with one), as the Methods say. The other three readings with the code's width give 29 to 30 and 24 to 27, the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: The periodic orbits are robust to the threshold for recurrence, with similar periodicity at thresholds of 10%, 5% and 2%.
outcomes.source: Figure 2, figure supplement 2; Materials and methods, Recurrence analysis, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: similar periodicity of recurrence was maintained at all tested thresholds from 2% upwards
outcomes.notes: Reading (a) holds for both lower thresholds under every reading of width, count and period (Spearman 0.70 to 0.97, all p below 2e-5, 30 responses with a peak at both thresholds). Reading (b) holds at 5% in all eight cases and fails at 2% in six (adopted, mean period, median absolute difference 1.30 s against 1.27 s).

outcomes.statement: Almost all evoked responses reach a state of high recurrence within one oscillation period of stimulation and are thereafter dominated by recurrence.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity meets the conditions for a periodic attractor, paragraph 2; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: We found that almost all evoked population responses quickly reached a state of high recurrence, within one oscillation period ( Figure 3A ), and were thereafter dominated by recurrence
outcomes.notes: Coalescence (first window with at least 90% recurrent points) within one dominant period of onset in 12 of 30 responses (adopted reading), 11 to 14 under the others, against 27 required; from offset 19 of 30 (17 to 20). Coalescence 7.5 to 49.5 s after onset, median 14.5 s. The stability part holds, more than 50% of points recur after coalescence in 30 of 30 (60.8% to 98.6%). As the checked points start 5 s after onset (Methods), the earliest possible coalescence is 7.5 s after onset, near the shortest periods (8.7 to 9.4 s). The lateness is not an edge effect of the 90% line, as within one period of onset the highest window density reaches 0.8 in 15 of 30 responses and 0.7 in 21.
deviations: A window counts as coalesced when at least 90% of its points recur, as the Methods say (Testing convergence to the same manifold); the code's PrctWnone below 10 is the strict form. With 500 points per window the two differ only at exactly 450 points; the counts are those of the strict form except from offset (19 against 18).

outcomes.statement: Sequentially evoked responses of a preparation fall on the same manifold; their distance is below that of random projections for all pairs except two, pairs (1,2) and (1,3) of preparation 4.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity meets the conditions for a periodic attractor, paragraph 4; Figure 3C legend
outcomes.quote: pairs of evoked population responses from the same preparation fell close to each other throughout ( Figure 3C ), well in excess of the expected agreement between random projections of the data onto the same embedding dimensions
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), recurrent points, 29 of 30 pairs below their control mean under every reading, failing pair (1,2) of preparation 4 (1.04 times its control). Reading (b), the code's point sets, 28 of 30 under every reading, failing pairs (1,2) and (1,3) of preparation 4 (1.19 and 1.17), the pairs the paper names. 100 shuffles each way; 2 s.e.m. of the control 0.11 to 0.36.
deviations: The Hausdorff distances use scipy's exact directed_hausdorff in place of the code's loops.

outcomes.statement: The convergence of sequential responses to the same manifold holds when the three programs are projected onto common axes from a PCA of their concatenated activity.
outcomes.source: Figure 3, figure supplement 1A
outcomes.quote: We obtain the same results: sequentially-evoked programs converge to the same manifold
outcomes.notes: On common axes (5 to 10 PCs, at most 80%), recurrent points 30 of 30 under every reading; the code's point sets 28 of 30 (failing preparation 4, pairs (1,2) and (1,3)) under three readings and 27 under own/le80 (also preparation 8, pair (2,3)).

outcomes.statement: Stimulation drives responses of the same preparation far apart before coalescence, more than at stimulus onset or after both have coalesced, so the same manifold is reached from different initial conditions.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity meets the conditions for a periodic attractor, paragraph 5; Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: We found that the stimulation caused population responses within the same preparation to diverge far more than in either the spontaneous activity or after coalescing to the manifold ( Figure 3D )
outcomes.notes: The transient distance exceeds both the onset and the coalesced distance in 30 of 30 pairs under every reading and both point sets. Adopted reading, medians 9.31 (onset), 45.44 (transient) and 14.51 (coalesced, code's point sets).
deviations: The transient distance uses every fifth point of the second program of the pair, to save time; points 10 ms apart are nearly equal, so the maximum changes little.

outcomes.statement: Pairwise similarity between neurons is preserved across responses of the same preparation, above a null model, except for pairs (1,3) and (2,3) of preparation 7.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity meets the conditions for a periodic attractor, paragraph 6; Figure 3F legend
outcomes.quote: We found that pair-wise similarity is indeed well-preserved across population responses in the same preparation ( Figure 3F )
outcomes.notes: Data correlation above control in 29 of 30 pairs (Spearman, first program's control), 30 (Pearson, first), 27 (Spearman, larger control) and 28 (Pearson, larger control), the same under every reading of width and count. With Pearson and the larger control the failing pairs are (1,3) and (2,3) of preparation 7, as the paper names them; with Spearman and the first control pair (1,3) of preparation 4 fails (0.597 against 0.622).
deviations: The similarity matrix is the correlation of the post-onset spike-density functions, as the criterion says; the code takes it from its clustering toolbox's convolved trains, which use the same kernel width.

outcomes.statement: Of 19 spontaneous divergences from the trajectory, 17 (90%) returned to a recurrent state; the two that did not were consistent with the end of the evoked locomotion.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity meets the conditions for a periodic attractor, paragraph 7; Materials and methods, Testing return to the same manifold after perturbation; Figure 3H
outcomes.quote: For the remaining 19 divergent periods, we then determined if the population activity returned to a recurrent state after the divergent point; that is, whether the density of recurrence returned above 90% or not. The majority (17/19) did
outcomes.notes: Adopted reading with the Methods' period (mean of the peak), 34 divergent periods, 16 kept after removing those within two periods of the end, 15 returned (0.938). The fraction meets the criterion and both counts fall just below their tolerances (17.1 to 20.9 and 15.3 to 18.7). With the median of the peak (the code's period) 17 kept and 16 returned (0.941); 16 returns are within tolerance and 17 periods just below 17.1. Over the four readings 14 to 19 kept, 13 to 17 returned, fractions 0.875 to 0.941; the counts meet the criterion only under own/le80 (18 kept and 16 returned with the mean period, 19 and 17 with the median). With eight combinations run, a pass under one of them is weak evidence. The code's rule, removing only the periods within two cycles of the end that never return, keeps 17 to 21 over the readings; under the adopted reading it keeps 19 of which 18 return (0.947), with either period, which meets both tolerances and matches the paper's 19. The criterion states the Methods' rule ("We removed all such divergent periods whose divergent point fell within two oscillation cycles of the end of the recording"), so the code's rule is reported, not judged. The criterion has no partial outcome; partially reproduced is kept because the returned fraction holds and the two counts miss their tolerances by 1.1 and 0.3.
deviations: Divergent periods follow the Methods' definition (runs of windows below 90% after coalescence that fall below 50%), computed directly; the code's loop in recurrence_point_results_Viz.m finds the same kind of run.

Assumed, the adopted reading (own/min80) and the period for the two-cycle rule, the Methods' mean of the dominant peak. The outcome is reproduced only under own/le80. Question for the authors under findings.

outcomes.statement: Of the 17 divergences that returned to a recurrent state, all but three returned to the same manifold; the three appeared to move to a different periodic attractor.
outcomes.source: Results, Joint population activity meets the conditions for a periodic attractor, paragraph 7; Figure 3I
outcomes.quote: Of those that returned, all but three clearly returned to the same manifold ( Figure 3I )
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), recurrences after the divergent point (the code's blnSame), 13 of the 15 returned divergences exceed 0.2 under the adopted reading, within 12.6 to 15.4; reading (a), after the end of the divergent period (Methods), 10. With the median period 14 of 16 under (b) and 11 under (a). Over the four readings (b) gives 11 to 17 and (a) 9 to 14. It depends on claim fig3h-perturbations-return, whose counts are just short; the returned divergences tested here are those it finds. The count depends strongly on the reading (9 to 17), so the pass under the adopted reading is weak evidence for the paper's 14.

outcomes.statement: The evoked responses have highly clustered maximum eigenvalues of the local linear dynamics, dominated by negative complex values, so the pedal ganglion implements a contracting periodic orbit, a stable spiral attractor, found in every preparation.
outcomes.source: Results, Heterogenous population activity arises from a common attractor, paragraph 2; Introduction, last paragraph; Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: Doing so, we found that the evoked population responses had highly clustered maximum eigenvalues ( Figure 4B,C ), and thus highly similar underlying dynamics ... The dominance of negative complex eigenvalues implies the pedal ganglion network implements a contracting periodic orbit - it is a stable spiral attractor
outcomes.notes: The grand mean is a stable spiral under every reading (adopted a = -0.000362, b = 0.00729). 21 of 30 responses lie in the stable-spiral region; 8 of 10 preparations have at least two of three (preparations 3 and 4 have one each); other readings 20 to 23 responses and 6 to 9 preparations. Spread, SD of a 0.00058 and of b 0.0028 across responses. No point of a dominant orbit had fewer than 100 neighbours (fewest in any response 195, median of the per-response medians 1566), so the filter removes nothing here.
deviations: The maximum eigenvalue is the one of largest modulus, as MATLAB's max orders complex numbers in LocalLinearDynamics.m; the Methods do not say how the maximum is taken.

The local neighbourhood is the contiguous run of points within 2.5 theta around the point, as the Methods describe. The code's run detection subtracts the point's position in the neighbourhood from the time indices (abs(currixs - ixPt)), which can miss gaps before the point; that quirk is not reproduced.

outcomes.statement: The linear model estimates a mean orbital period of about 10 s, consistent with the period from the recurrent points.
outcomes.source: Results, Heterogenous population activity arises from a common attractor, paragraph 5; Figure 4C
outcomes.quote: The linear model estimated a mean orbital period of around 10 s ( Figure 4C ), consistent with the directly-derived estimate from the recurrent points ( Figure 2F )
outcomes.notes: Mean over responses of 2 pi / b times 0.01 s, 10.45 s under the adopted reading; the variant mean of per-point rotation periods 10.24 s. With count (ii) (the code's) 13.55 s (own/le80) and 12.22 s (pooled/le80), outside tolerance. The per-response linear periods do not correlate with the recurrence periods (Pearson r = -0.063, p = 0.74; -0.12 to 0.03 under the other readings), and the means do not agree within the claim's tolerance either (10.45 s against a median recurrence period of 12.73 s, 2.3 s apart where the tolerance is 1 s). The criterion judges the mean and reports the correlation, so "consistent with" is reported, not judged; neither the correlation nor the means support it.
deviations: Assumed, the Methods' count rule (smallest number of PCs reaching 80%); the code's rule gives a mean period outside the tolerance. Question for the authors under findings.

outcomes.statement: In most responses the trajectory contracts in all embedding dimensions; a few responses have a positive real eigenvalue in one low-variance dimension, a minor expansion.
outcomes.source: Results, Heterogenous population activity arises from a common attractor, paragraph 3; Figure 4, figure supplement 1A
outcomes.quote: In most population responses, the low-dimensional trajectory had negative, complex eigenvalues in all embedding dimensions ... Intriguingly, a few population responses had a positive real eigenvalue in one low-variance dimension
outcomes.notes: All unique-dimension means negative in 11 of 30 responses (8 to 11 under the other readings), where more than 15 are required. The second part holds, 10 responses (9 to 12) have exactly one positive mean, in a dimension other than the first. In 7 responses the first dimension's mean is positive.

outcomes.statement: Local trajectories were dominated by rotation throughout; in every preparation most local models have a complex eigenvalue among their top two.
outcomes.source: Figure 4, figure supplement 1B
outcomes.quote: Population responses were dominated by rotation throughout
outcomes.notes: Proportion of local models with a complex eigenvalue among the top two above 0.5 in all 30 responses under every reading (adopted 0.87 to 1.00).

outcomes.statement: Over a response the orbital period may slow, speed up or not change; all three occur among the 30 responses.
outcomes.source: Results, Heterogenous population activity arises from a common attractor, paragraph 5; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: We found that the population responses included all possible changes in periodic orbit: slowing, speeding up, and not changing ( Figure 5B )
outcomes.notes: Adopted reading, 12 slowing, 4 speeding and 14 unchanged at p < 0.01 (10000 permutations of the window delays, two-sided); the code's pooled one-sided test with 100000 permutations gives 13, 4 and 13. Windows per response 31 to 73, from the first to the last window with at least 90% recurrent points. Other readings 10 to 14 slowing, 4 to 6 speeding, 11 to 15 unchanged.
deviations: The Methods do not say what the permutation test permutes; the main test permutes the mean delays against window time, keeping the weights with the windows, and is two-sided. The code's test, which permutes the pooled time and delay values and is one-sided, is shown as the claims file's variant. Ranks are assigned without averaging ties, as in WeightedCorrelation.m.

outcomes.statement: There is no relationship between the change in orbital period over a response and its rate of contraction, as a stable spiral predicts.
outcomes.source: Results, Heterogenous population activity arises from a common attractor, paragraph 5; Figure 5C legend
outcomes.quote: As predicted there was no relationship between the contraction of the periodic orbit and its change in period ( Figure 5C )
outcomes.notes: Pearson R = -0.341, p = 0.065 between weighted rho and mean real part (adopted reading); -0.342, p = 0.064 with the contraction in %/s. Other readings R = -0.14 to -0.34, p = 0.064 to 0.46. No relation at p < 0.05, but the effect is moderate and p is near the threshold.

outcomes.statement: No recorded neuron is a P10 motorneuron; no neuron comes close to one-to-one locking of its spikes with P10 spikes at any delay, nor locks consistently across programs.
outcomes.source: Figure 6, figure supplement 1; Materials and methods, Decoding motor output, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We see that no neuron in our dataset comes close to P ( s p i k e 10 | s p i k e ) ≈ 1 at any delay, and there are no neurons with consistently high locking between programs
outcomes.notes: 1050 neuron-program values (1 neuron without spikes after 33 s); largest maximum locking 0.522; none at 0.9 or more, none in two programs; 2 values reach 0.5, none 0.7.

outcomes.statement: P10 nerve activity can be fitted and forecast from the low-dimensional trajectory in all nine responses with P10 recordings, so the trajectory encodes muscle commands.
outcomes.source: Results, The locomotion motor program can be decoded from the low-dimensional orbit, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 6B to 6D
outcomes.quote: The model could accurately fit and forecast P10 activity from the low-dimensional trajectory in all nine population responses ( Figure 6D )
outcomes.notes: Methods' windowing, mean forecast R minus 2 s.e.m. above 0 in 8 of 9 responses under every reading of width and count (adopted, mean R of the other eight 0.36 to 0.89); the criterion requires each of the nine and has no partial rule. Response 1 of preparation 4 fails under all four (mean R -0.060, -0.120, -0.080 and -0.123 for own/min80, own/le80, pooled/min80 and pooled/le80; bounds -0.127 to -0.204), with histories up to 100 ms, and with the code's windowing (mean R -0.102, bound -0.131). Its training fit is good (mean training R 0.94; 0.91 to 0.97 in all nine) but its forecasts are not, forecast R -0.59 to 0.27 in four windows plotted, against 0.81 to 0.94 for response 2 of the same preparation. Forecast windows, 40 per response with the Methods' windowing (360), 174 per response with the code's (1566); the paper's N = 173 is close to the code's count per response. The failing response is the one the paper describes as apparently chaotic. The decoding gives different numbers in different executions, as forecasts diverge in some windows of the longer histories (in the executed copy, 462 to 627 of 5760 windows over all histories with the Methods' windowing, 1614 of 7830 with the code's, above 10 times the response's largest P10 rate, up to about 1e13 spikes/s at the clip of the linear predictor; one window of the selected histories, under pooled/min80). The copy reviewed in round 3 gave mean R -0.060, -0.127, -0.060 and -0.119 for that response and -0.101 with the code's windowing; the pass counts were 8 of 9 under every reading in each execution. A perturbation of the PCs by 1e-9 of their SD changes the mean MAE of preparation 4, bout 1 at 150 ms with the code's windowing from 5.3e11 to 4.2e11 and leaves the 50 ms model nearly unchanged (13.27 and 13.32), so mean MAEs with diverging windows, and the history selected from them, depend on rounding; the forecast R of the selected models moves by up to 0.02 between executions.
deviations: The Poisson GLM is fitted by a numpy IRLS in place of MATLAB's glmfit, at most 25 iterations with a relative deviance change of 1e-6 (a standard choice; the forecasts of one program agreed to three decimals with 100 iterations).
Each window's fit starts from the previous window's coefficients, which changes only the starting point of the iterations.
All four readings of width and count with the code's width are run with the Methods' windowing; the variants (histories up to 100 ms, the code's windowing) under the adopted reading.

outcomes.statement: The nine recordings with P10 activity need only 3 to 5 embedding dimensions for 80% variance, and at least double that for 90%; using the 90% dimensions does not improve the P10 forecasts.
outcomes.source: Results, The locomotion motor program can be decoded from the low-dimensional orbit, paragraph 4; Figure 6, figure supplement 2
outcomes.quote: The successful decoding of future P10 activity was achieved despite needing only 3–5 embedding dimensions to account for 80% variance ... Increasing the number of embedding dimensions to account for 90% variance, at least doubling the number of embedding dimensions, did not improve the forecasts of P10 activity
outcomes.notes: Reproduced under own/le80, where both parts hold. The nine 80% counts are 3 to 5 under own/le80 and pooled/le80, and the 90% counts at least double them in each. Under own/le80 with the full history grid for both, the 90% models are not better, mean MAE lower in 5 of 9 (two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.91, median difference -0.13) and mean R-squared higher in 4 of 9 (p = 0.50). Under pooled/le80 (four histories) p = 0.65 and 0.82. Under the adopted reading (own/min80) the counts are 4 to 6 and one (6) is outside 2.7 to 5.5; there the 90% models are worse in MAE (p = 0.027, 7 of 9 worse, full grid; p = 0.020 with four histories for both) and do not differ in R-squared (p = 0.13). No comparison finds the 90% models better at p < 0.05. Over all histories 1111 (own/le80) and 1166 (own/min80) of 5760 windows of the 90% models have diverging forecasts in the executed copy, so the mean MAEs and these p-values depend on rounding through the history selected and differ between executions; earlier executions gave p = 0.50 and 0.91 for MAE under own/le80, with the same conclusion.
deviations: The 90% models use the Methods' full history grid under own/min80 and own/le80, and histories of 50, 100, 150 and 200 ms under pooled/le80, to fit the time limit; the comparison is also shown with the 80% models restricted to the same four histories.

outcomes.statement: Every response has a long-tailed distribution of single-neuron participation, a minority of neurons dominating its dynamics.
outcomes.source: Results, Variable neuron participation in stable motor programs, paragraph 2; Figure 7A
outcomes.quote: Every population response had a long-tailed distribution of participation ( Figure 7A ), indicating that a minority of neurons dominated the dynamics of any given response
outcomes.notes: Both readings of d, 30 of 30 responses with positive skewness (0.50 to 4.36, reading (a)) and fewer than half the neurons above 50% of the maximum (at most 39.4%).
deviations: Participation uses the adopted kernel width (the recording's median ISI).

outcomes.statement: Neurons with high participation in one response often have low participation in another; every preparation contains neurons whose change in participation well exceeds that predicted by a noise model.
outcomes.source: Results, Variable neuron participation in stable motor programs, paragraph 2; Figure 7B to 7F
outcomes.quote: Every preparation’s pedal ganglion contained neurons whose change in participation between responses well-exceeded that predicted by the noise model ( Figure 7F )
outcomes.notes: All 10 preparations have strongly variable neurons under both readings of d and both poolings; reading (a) with all pairs at least 4 per preparation, 3.8% to 23.4% of neurons; consecutive pairs 5.9% to 29.3%.
deviations: Neuron ids are taken to name the same neuron in all bouts, as the data description says (recordings concatenated before spike sorting); per-neuron spike counts correlate between bouts above permuted ids in 30 of 30 pairs, which is consistent with it.

outcomes.statement: Even the most strongly participating neurons in a response could more than halve their participation in other evoked responses.
outcomes.source: Discussion, Insights and challenges of variable neuron participation, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Even the most strongly participating neurons in a given population response could more than halve their participation in other evoked responses
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), the neuron at 100%, halves in another program in 6 of 10 preparations; reading (b), the top 10%, in 9 of 10; the same under both readings of d.

outcomes.statement: A neuron's participation reflects both its firing rate and its synchrony; firing rate explains on average 50% of the variation in participation within a response, and rate changes 23% of the change in participation between responses.
outcomes.source: Figure 7, figure supplement 1B and 1D
outcomes.quote: Firing rate explains on average (R 2 , red line) 50% of the variation in participation within an evoked response ... Firing rate changes explain on average 23% of the variation in the change of participation
outcomes.notes: Participation (a), rate from stimulation offset, matched pairs, mean R-squared 0.491 within responses and 0.239 for changes. Rate from onset 0.514 and 0.265; the code's mismatched pairing 0.205 and 0.221; participation (b) 0.499 and 0.244.

outcomes.statement: The distance between a pair of responses does not correlate with the total change in neuron participation between them nor with the distance between their participation distributions; the program is robust to the participation of single neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Variable neuron participation in stable motor programs, paragraph 4; Figure 7G and 7H
outcomes.quote: We found that the distance between a pair of population responses did not correlate with either the total change in neuron participation between the two responses ( Figure 7G ) or the distance between their participation distributions ( Figure 7H )
outcomes.notes: Adopted width and count. With recurrent points the normalised distance rises with the total change in participation (slope 0.0127, p = 0.031, R-squared 0.17, 28 pairs) but not the Hellinger distance (p = 0.35); with the code's point sets it rises with the Hellinger distance (p = 0.028) but not the total change (p = 0.11). Participation reading (b) gives the same pattern (p = 0.032 and 0.017). So one of the two absences holds and the other fails, and the claim holds in part. Under own/le80 one slope is significant with the recurrent points (total change, p = 0.036) and none with the code's points (lowest p 0.053); under pooled/min80 and pooled/le80, with participation from the pooled width, no slope is significant with the legend's exclusion (lowest p 0.085 and 0.069). With the code's exclusion (pairs with normalised distance below 1), pooled/min80 has a significant total-change slope with the recurrent points (p = 0.028 and 0.029, participation readings (a) and (b)) and pooled/le80 has none (lowest p 0.069). The robust fits agree with the ordinary ones in significance except one (code points, adopted reading, reading (a), Hellinger, robust p = 0.063).
deviations: Assumed, the adopted reading of width and count (own/min80). Under the pooled readings the claim is reproduced with the legend's exclusion; with the code's exclusion pooled/min80 has one significant slope (total change, recurrent points). Participation is computed under each reading's width and count. The test is the code's linear regression slope, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: No small invariant core of strongly participating, phasically active neurons, such as a classic central pattern generator, is found across preparations.
outcomes.source: Results, Variable neuron participation in stable motor programs, paragraph 3; Figure 7, figure supplement 2
outcomes.quote: in our observed portion of the ganglion we found no evidence for a core of strongly participating, invariant, and phasically active neurons across the preparations
outcomes.notes: With a port of the code's ensemble toolbox, every preparation has neurons typed oscillator in all three programs (16 to 84 per preparation, adopted width, seed 7). The top 10% of them by maximum participation (2 to 8 neurons) have a median maximum change between consecutive programs of 0.068 to 0.440 of the program maximum, so only preparation 2 has an invariant core by the claims file's rule (1 of 10). Both widths, two seeds and both participation readings give 0 or 1 of 10. Without typing, the top 10% of all neurons have median maximum changes of 0.12 to 0.32, under 0.1 in none. The legend's statement that only the oscillator class had a consistently typed neuron in all ten preparations holds in part, as persistent oscillators are found in 10 of 10 under every variant but persistent bursters in 6 to 10 (10 in one variant).
deviations: The ensembles and types come from a Python port in apl.py of StaticEnsembles.m, consensus_cluster_spike_data_binless.m, allevsplitConTransitive.m, Analyse_Spike_Train_Properties.m (with shuffle_intervals.m and spike_xcorr.m) and Types_of_Ensemble_Across_Dataset.m at the cited commit, with the code's parameters. MATLAB's kmeans is replaced by Lloyd's algorithm from the code's k-means++ start; the port was not checked against MATLAB output. The clustering is random, so two seeds are shown.
The convolution kernel uses the recording's own median ISI (the code's Data.GaussSD, the adopted width) and, as a variant, the pooled width.

outcomes.statement: Neurons with strong participation across the three responses, and those with highly variable participation, lie mainly in the caudo-lateral quadrant of the ganglion.
outcomes.source: Results, Participation maps identify potential locations of the pattern generator network, paragraph 1; Figure 8
outcomes.quote: We found that neurons with strong participation across the three evoked population responses were robustly located in the caudo-lateral quadrant of the ganglion ( Figure 8A,B )
outcomes.notes: The criterion needs the orientation of the array. The paper's text, the code (ParticipationMapsSummary.m plots the coordinates on the diode template without labels), the data description and the files (Coordinates.mat, diode_template.mat, plot_maps.m) do not say which direction of x or y is rostral, caudal, medial or lateral. The notebook prints the counts of top-fifth neurons by quadrant of the array coordinates, which decide nothing without it. Shown for the verifier, not judged, the top-fifth neurons of each side concentrate in one quadrant of the array coordinates, the same for maximum under both divisions and for range under true quintiles (left x-y-, right x-y+); under true quintiles that quadrant holds 34% to 41% of the top fifth against 19% to 20% of all neurons, and under the code's equal-width fifths 71% (left, maximum, 15 of 21) and 54% (right, 15 of 28). The code's equal-width division leaves 1 or 2 neurons in the top fifth of the range, so that half of the test is nearly empty as the code defines it.

findings.statement: Coordinates.mat gives each neuron's x and y on a 0 to 50 scale without a unit, and neither the files, plot_maps.m nor the data description say which directions of the array are rostral, caudal, medial or lateral, so the paper's caudo-lateral quadrant cannot be located.
The P10 spike times are on a grid of 0.614 ms (1629.7 Hz), which agrees with the data description's 1630 Hz sampling; the paper says 1600 Hz.
The P10 files of preparation 2 are named Jun0414da0Np10.mat while its spike and coordinate files are Jun0414B; they can be matched only by the first seven characters, as the paper's code does.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier listed the archive, read the paper's code and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. Its report gave its own outcome for each claim; 24 of 30 agree with the record as it then stood.

disagreements.reason: Own/le80: 18 kept with 16 returned (mean period) and 19 kept with 17 returned (median period), both within tolerance. It fails under the adopted own/min80 reading (16 kept, 15 returned) and under the pooled readings. B.4: fig3h and fig3i are reading-shopped; eight readings were run, the target counts are met in only a few of them and not under the adopted reading, and this success is weak evidence.

The mean linear-model period is 10.45 s (own/min80) and 10.12 s (pooled/min80), within 10 plus or minus 1, but 13.55 s and 12.22 s under le80, the count under which fig2b holds. It is uncorrelated with the recurrence periods (r = -0.06, p = 0.74), so consistent with is not supported.

Mean R minus 2 s.e.m. is above 0 in 8 of 9 responses under all three windowings. Preparation 4, bout 1 has mean forecast R = -0.06. B.3: fig6d was decoded only under own/min80 (decode_program hard-codes min80); the le80 and pooled readings were not run, so it is unknown whether preparation 4, bout 1 fails under every reading. C: decoding under own/le80 and pooled/le80, plus a plot of P10 against the forecast for preparation 4, bout 1, would settle it.

Under le80, all 9 counts lie in 2.7 to 5.5 and the 90% count is at least twice the 80% count. The 90% models are not better: MAE is worse (p = 0.0195, 7 of 9 worse) and R-squared does not differ (p = 0.25). B.5: the 90% models search only 50, 100, 150 and 200 ms while the 80% models search 50 to 200 ms in 10 ms steps, which favours the 80% models; a like-for-like comparison was available from by_history but was not shown. B.6: the counts pass only under le80, but the forecasts compare min80 against min90 dimensions.

Adopted own/min80, one slope is significant with recurrent points (total change, p = 0.031) and one with the code's points (Hellinger, p = 0.028). Under pooled/le80 neither slope is significant. B.2: fig7gh was run under only 2 of the 4 readings; own/le80 and pooled/min80 are missing, and the outcome flips between the two readings that were run.

Cell 71 is a placeholder; nothing was computed. B.8: fig7s2 is labelled blocked although it is testable; the archive holds all 30 spike-time sets, which is everything the ensemble typing needs, the paper links the code toolbox and the claims file names those scripts. A partial test is also possible with no typing, the top 10% by maximum participation and their median maximum change, from PART.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the attempt record and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier found no place where the claims file misreads the paper and agreed with 29 of the 30 outcomes. It also noted that the README gives about 36 minutes where the notebook printed 33.8 min (now about 40 minutes; this revision's run printed 39.6 min).

disagreements.reason: The criterion requires mean forecast R minus 2 s.e.m. above 0 in each of the nine responses, and it has no partial rule; the paper's statement is specifically in all nine. Cell 79 shows preparation 4, bout 1 failing under all four readings, with histories up to 100 ms, and with the code's windowing (mean R -0.060 to -0.127), so the failure does not depend on the reading. Eight of nine is a failure of exactly what the claim says, not a partial match. In cells 79 and 83 (not discussed anywhere) the mean MAE for preparation 4, bout 1 reaches 7.6e6 with the code's windowing, which points to exploding forecasts in some windows.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 3. The proposed change of outcome of fig6d-decode-p10, the only one in the record, with the analysis behind it in the full executed notebook of the second revision and the claims file. The verifier found that the claims file does not misread the paper here. It also found that the numbers of the record's reason and notes and of the fig6d conclusion do not match that notebook's outputs, without changing the outcome.

paper_notes.statement: The paper gives 120 to 180 neurons per recorded population and 1131 neurons in all over 10 preparations; ten preparations of at least 120 would hold at least 1200. The data set holds 75 to 160 neurons per preparation, 1131 in all, as its description says.

Question for the authors. The Methods give the Gaussian width as the median ISI divided by 12 (the extracted text; possibly the square root of 12), but the code uses the median ISI itself, computed as a running median over the recordings of the same bout number read so far. With median ISI / 12 or / sqrt(12) the recordings need 21 to 76 PCs for 80% of the variance, not the paper's 4 to 8. Which width was used for the published figures, and was the median meant to be per recording?

Question for the authors. The Methods say the projection kept the dimensions needed for at least 80% of the variance; the recurrence and participation code keeps those whose cumulative variance is at most 80% (one fewer), while the manifold code keeps the smallest number reaching 80%. Which rule produced Figures 2 to 5? The linear-model period of Figure 4C is 10.45 s under the first and 12.2 to 13.6 s under the second.

Question for the authors. For removing divergent periods within two oscillation cycles of the end, is the cycle the mean or the median recurrence time of the dominant peak, and is the rule applied to all divergent periods (Methods) or only to those that never return (code)? The counts change from 16 to 21 kept periods with these choices.

Question for the authors. The permutation test of the weighted Spearman correlation (Tracking changes in periodicity) is not described beyond 10000 permutations; the code permutes the pooled time and period values with 100000 permutations and tests one side. Which test gave Figure 5B?

Figure 6D reports N = 173 forecast windows. The Methods' windowing (40 s fit, 10 s forecast, 1 s steps from 33 s) gives 40 windows per response here; the code's windowing (training on 50% of the series, 0.2 s steps) gives 174 per response, close to 173, so the figure appears to use the code's windowing, not the Methods'.

In What_is_Participation.m the rate changes are ordered (1,2), (1,3), (2,3) and the participation changes (1,2), (2,3), (1,3), so two of three pairs are mismatched in the correlation behind Figure 7, figure supplement 1D. With matched pairs the mean R-squared is 0.239, with the code's pairing 0.205.

LocalLinearDynamics.m finds the contiguous neighbourhood of a point from abs(currixs - ixPt), the time indices minus the point's position within the neighbourhood, so gaps among neighbours earlier than that position are not detected and the fitted run can extend past them. The Methods describe a run contiguous in time.

entries.name: bruno-2017
entries.title: Spiral attractor in the Aplysia pedal ganglion (Bruno, Frost and Humphries 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Bruno, Frost and Humphries (2017) on CRCNS data set apl-1, which holds the spike times of 30 voltage-sensitive dye recordings of the pedal ganglion (three evoked bouts of fictive locomotion in each of 10 preparations), the P10 nerve spikes of nine of them and the neurons' positions on the photodiode array. It ports the paper's recurrence analysis, local linear models, manifold comparisons, P10 decoding, participation measures and ensemble typing from the paper's MATLAB code, under every reading of the kernel width and the number of dimensions.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Bruno, Frost and Humphries (2017) from CRCNS apl-1
